name: VAllhalla
_about: VAllhalla 1.0.0: at work (the game's room "bar", or while someone talks on a break) the stand-by overlay is our own drawn bar window (bg_bar_window.png) with Jill right of centre and the counter (bar_counter.png, tools/gen_bar_counter.py) in front of her with her shadow from the neon wall on it (bar_shadow.png, drawn twice: va_shadow_l / _r stretch its left and right edges out now and then, each on its own); the light on the rest of the counter top dips with the flicker (bar_top_dim.png), the shadow doesn't; a violet dimmer over the window's lit middle (bg_neon_dim.png, tools/gen_neon_dim.py) calms its cyan and flickers like a neon now and then (va_neon), with a neon tube down the middle of the light (bg_neon_tube.png) that flickers with it, its light blurred over the shelves (bg_neon_bloom.png) and 24 specks of dust drifting up through it (neon_mote.png, va_mote<i>_x/_y/_a). At home, on the break screen and anywhere else the stand-by screen shows the title screen's Jill (jilltitle_spr, animated), (menus and loading too), or the back street (break_bg1) when Jill walks out of the bar for her break, a pixel dissolve between any two of them, "Please Stand by" under it (va_room / va_jill_scene / va_doodles: the module reads the runner's room). The drink just served (its sprite from the player's game, or the glitched bottle) slides onto Jill's counter from the right with its own shadow, bubbles rising in its liquid, (shadow7: its silhouette flipped and squashed, leaning away from the neon), fades with the overlay like Jill, and stays until the next order is mixed. A tap on Jill's scene is the next line (the module puts the game's cursor on the text box, then presses A), not on the stand-by screen nor with the jukebox up. Jill (the game's jill_* portrait sprites, loaded from the player's game.win) replaces the doodles on the stand-by overlay; her mouth moves while her line types out, she blinks, and her face follows the scene (the module finds the line on screen in the player's own script files; faces from the game's tags plus our tables for every day, the tutorial, the epilogues, game over and the 1.2 scenes). ships no game art and no art taken from elsewhere. The frame is drawn from code; labels use Eden Duo's font; the cans, shaker, Ice/Age, Reset/Mix/Slot sprites and their hover versions are read from the player's own copy of the game at runtime by the native module. The artist's own work ships: the SUCCESS popup, the error windows, the tutorial hand and filters (see CREDITS.txt). The money of the night (global.barscore) sits above Ice, and the Slot buttons follow the game's two slots on the nights with two customers (the game's slot sprites; a tap switches the slot, the bar shows slot 2's own shaker, and both drinks of a two-slot order stand on Jill's counter, the second one right of her). An easter egg: the little heart under Age says the game's "itai!" when tapped, and opens a note from the artist on the third tap. The meters are the game's own cells (a_on..e_on / abig_on..ebig_on), and each pour flashes its colour's outline round the shaker (shakerpulse_*). Mechanics as 0.15: drag-to-pour, meters, Ice/Age, automatic talking/mixing lock, manual shake with blend bar. Text uses PixelMplus12 (the free font the game itself uses; M+ FONT LICENSE, see LICENSE-PixelMplus.txt), decoded by the module's font extension. 0.17: the companion works out the drink from what was poured on the bottom screen, Ice, Age and the shake time (the game's recipe list, Big = doubled), shows that drink's sprite from the player's game in place of the shaker with SUCCESS, or the broken glass with FAILED, until the drink is served or Reset. 0.18: a failed drink pops up the artist's ERROR! window 4 times in three sizes around the shaker (with her glitch frames); the bar stays blocked until each one is tapped away. After a successful drink the Mix button turns into a green Serve button (the game's button, recoloured on the device). While the shaker is held it shows only in the player's finger (its spot on the panel is empty), swinging as it mixes. The shaker can only be picked up once something has been poured into it. After a failed drink everything but Reset is locked (like the game), Mix is greyed out, and once the error windows are closed the Reset button pulses. Cans have a bigger grab area and the shaker a bigger drop area. The shaker only mixes while you shake it: stop and the drink is mixed; 5 s of non-stop shaking blends it. The shaker leans the way your finger moves and wobbles back upright. Every drink shows its own sprite by exact name. Meters, Ice and Aging follow the game itself, whatever you pour with. Mix button mixes like the game: the shaker shakes by itself, tap Stop to finish (5 s = blended). Reset in the game also clears the bottom screen's drink and errors. ZR in the game also shakes the bottom shaker. The bottled A Fedora counts as a drink. 0.20.13: while the bar is locked (dialogue), the game's own break-screen doodles (break_skin, read from the player's copy) play over the purple overlay (the break screen's phone and its icons cut out). 0.20.15/16: Reset in the middle of a mix stops the shaking and empties the bottom shaker (and stops the game's mix too if it kept going); while the shaker shakes by itself only Reset and Stop work, like the game; a mix the game never starts (ZR ignored while the left stick is held) stops on the bottom screen too. Reset in the game (ZL) in the middle of a mix stops and empties the bottom shaker too. 0.21.0: a one-time manual-shake tutorial on the first pour: the bar dims and locks around the shaker, a ring and a floating hand point at it with the text "In this version of the game, you can manually grab the shaker to mix or blend. Try it out!!!"; it ends (and is remembered across updates) once a shake starts a mix. The ring and hand are placeholders. 0.22.0: a one-time failed-drink tutorial: the first time the error windows pop up, the bar dims under them, the floating hand points at the big one and a window says "Oh no!! It seems that you did a mistake, get rid of those errors by tapping on them"; it ends (and is remembered) once every window is closed. 0.23.0: the tutorials come back every session until they are finished and the game is then saved: finishing one hides it for the session, and the first in-game save after that keeps it hidden on this device (the module spots a save by the new save time the game writes into memory). 0.24.0: loading a save (the in-game Load) starts the tutorials over unless they were kept by a save. 0.25.0: the tutorials as the mockups: a dithered filter over the bar (with a hole for the shaker), the player's own blue doodle head (break_skin, animated) bottom left, the artist's pointing hand, and the text in a black window. 0.26.0: the game's own sounds for the companion's own mechanics, through a load-time hook in the game's interpreter (guest/<build>/load-plan.json, tools/gen_load_plan.py): the ice rattles (iceadd) on every swing of a hand-held shaker, louder the harder it is shaken, and closing an error window clicks (click_sound). No audio ships with the package.
